speaker: Doctor
text:
Let me start by asking: How long have you been experiencing joint pain, and which specific joints are affected? 

REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count

speaker: Patient
text: 69-year-old male. The patient presents with pain in his left great toe, hips, and knees that worsens with activity and improves with rest. He reports that the symptoms have progressively gotten worse over the past several years.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left great toe, hips, and knees. I also have Symptoms worsen with activity, Symptoms improve with rest.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Obesity, type II diabetes mellitus, smoking history, hypertension. Social history: Drinks roughly ten beers per day. Recent travel history to Bangkok with unprotected sex.

speaker: Patient
text: Patient did not report any other systemic symptoms. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Cellulitis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is surprising, as cellulitis typically presents with red, warm, and swollen skin rather than chronic joint pain; can you describe the exact appearance of your skin around the affected joints? REQUEST TEST: Erythrocyte_Sedimentation_Rate (ESR)

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Gout (likely acute gouty arthritis or chronic tophaceous gout, as the normal ESR and lack of skin findings rule out cellulitis and septic arthritis, and the patient's history of a misdiagnosis suggests an inflammatory crystalline arthropathy).
